fixes.explanation: Quiet, yes. "He will quiet you with His love…" (Zephaniah 3:17) After all that talk of fear in this passage, I think that sounds like a gift. The same verse says, "He will rejoice over you with singing." Rejoicing, gladness and singing are all in that one verse.

I'd have bet on True too, so let me set it straight. The LORD says, "On that day you will not be put to shame for any of the deeds by which you have transgressed against Me." (Zephaniah 3:11) Those words say there is no shame on that day for any of those deeds.

Pride, yes. The LORD says, "…I will remove from among you those who rejoice in their pride, and you will never again be haughty on My holy mountain." (Zephaniah 3:11) Haughty means looking down on everybody. The ones who rejoice in their pride are the ones He takes out of the batch.

A meek and humble people, yes! The LORD says, "But I will leave within you a meek and humble people, and they will trust in the name of the LORD." (Zephaniah 3:12) The proud are removed, and the humble are the ones left standing. They are exactly who He keeps.

Standing guard is what you do when you figure trouble is coming. The text says, "But they will feed and lie down, with no one to make them tremble." (Zephaniah 3:13) Nobody is making them tremble, so there's no night shift in this picture. Feeding and lying down is the whole plan.

Their punishment, yes. "The LORD has taken away your punishment; He has turned back your enemy." (Zephaniah 3:15) That's the reason for all the shouting. When a weight like that is lifted, I'd be shouting too.

Land is a fair guess, but it isn't the word here. The text says, "The LORD has taken away your punishment…" (Zephaniah 3:15) He takes something away, and it's the punishment. That's the good news the call is singing about.
Test is a fair guess, but the verse says, "He will quiet you with His love…" (Zephaniah 3:17) Quiet is the word that fills the blank. It's a love that settles them, with rejoicing right alongside it.

Lame, yes, and that's the word. The LORD says, "I will save the lame and gather the scattered…" (Zephaniah 3:19) He names the lame right there in the promise, next to the scattered. He says plainly that He will save them.

The mighty seem like the easy ones to pick. But the LORD says, "I will save the lame and gather the scattered…" (Zephaniah 3:19) It's the lame He names. He is the one who will save them, and the scattered get gathered too.

That's the opposite of what He says, friend. The LORD says, "…I will appoint praise and fame for the disgraced throughout the earth." (Zephaniah 3:19) Praise and fame, not hiding. And it reaches throughout the earth.
